I am getting old now, 65 this year, and I farm alone since my family is not here. 18.8 mu is a lot for one man, so I must think carefully about what I can handle.

My land I divide like this: on about 13 mu I do the wheat-maize, same as always, same as my neighbors. The other 5.8 mu I plant cotton — the price is not so good these past years but I have grown it a long time and I know how. Cotton takes more work though, so I cannot plant more than this, my back cannot take it.

For the wheat I will put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer (复合肥) before planting, that is about 80-100 jin per mu, plus I will top-dress with urea (尿素) when it comes green in spring, maybe half a bag per mu. Last year this worked, wheat came out around 450 jin dry. I use the improved seed, the one the agricultural supply shop sells, jiamai or something like that, my neighbor Old Wang uses it too and he gets good grain. Water from the well — 3 times I water: one before winter, one when it turns green, one when the head fills out.

For maize after wheat, I put 1.5 bags of compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea at big trumpet stage. Hybrid seed, must use hybrid, nobody plants the old kind anymore. Maize I water 2 times from the well, sometimes 3 if the sky is dry. Last year about 550 jin per mu, that is good enough.

Cotton I know well, 45 years I have grown it. Compound fertilizer at planting, about 2 bags per mu because cotton eats a lot, and urea when it squares. Pesticide is many times for cotton — bollworm, aphid, red spider — maybe 6-7 sprays, cannot avoid. I use the hybrid seed too. I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose yield, fertilizer money you can calculate, but bad harvest is real loss.

Plough I do for wheat because we always plough, then rotary for maize since no time between wheat harvest and maize planting. Cotton I plough too in spring.
